item.title: Cowboys stun Texans with a last-minute comeback
item.description: CeeDee Lamb caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards and scored the winning 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left as Dallas erased a 20-point deficit to beat Houston 34-30. The Cowboys scored 28 points after halftime, while the Texans fell to 0-4.

item.title: Chiefs hold off Raiders to remain the AFC’s last unbeaten team
item.description: Patrick Mahomes threw for 225 yards and two touchdowns, while Kenneth Walker III ran for 177 yards and two scores as Kansas City beat Las Vegas 30-27. The Chiefs improved to 4-0 and became the AFC’s final unbeaten team; the Raiders took their first loss.

item.title: Valkyries take Game 1 from defending champion Aces
item.description: Gabby Williams had 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists as Golden State beat defending champion Las Vegas 71-60 in the franchise’s first WNBA semifinal game. Kiah Stokes added 14 rebounds and three blocks, and the Valkyries controlled the glass to seize a 1-0 series lead.

item.title: No. 25 Missouri routs No. 8 Florida
item.description: Missouri ended a nine-game losing streak against ranked opponents by overwhelming No. 8 Florida 45-17. The No. 25 Tigers forced four turnovers, built a 31-10 halftime lead and turned a matchup of ranked SEC teams into the weekend’s biggest top-10 upset.

item.title: White Sox blank Guardians in ALDS opener
item.description: Chicago opened the AL Division Series with a 3-0 win in Cleveland behind Munetaka Murakami’s homer and a combined three-hitter. Grant Taylor became the first postseason pitcher since 2017 to work at least four innings and earn a save, protecting the shutout after starter Shane Smith departed.

item.title: Verstappen wins rain-chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
item.description: A day after taking pole, Max Verstappen converted it into his first victory of the season as heavy rain, a delayed start and a late safety car scrambled the relocated Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang. Kimi Antonelli finished second, Lewis Hamilton third, and George Russell retired late as his title hopes faded.

item.title: NHL opening night brings new faces and late drama
item.description: Alex Tuch scored twice in his Washington debut as the Capitals beat defending champion Carolina 5-2. Elsewhere on the NHL’s first busy Friday, Boston erased a late deficit and beat Winnipeg in overtime, the Rangers and Blues posted shutouts, and Anaheim survived after building a four-goal lead in Las Vegas.

item.title: Three ranked road tests headline college football Saturday
item.description: Saturday’s schedule sends No. 5 Ohio State to No. 14 Iowa, No. 7 Alabama to No. 16 Mississippi State and No. 8 Florida to No. 25 Missouri. All three ranked home teams are coming off stirring victories. No. 4 Miami also visits Clemson, while unbeaten Cincinnati tries to reach 5-0 at Arizona.

item.title: Verstappen takes first pole of season at Sepang
item.description: Max Verstappen claimed his first Formula One pole of the season at Malaysia’s revived Sepang race, edging Lewis Hamilton in brutal heat. Isack Hadjar qualified third but drops to eighth because of a grid penalty, moving championship leader Kimi Antonelli alongside Charles Leclerc on the second row.

item.title: Braves win decisive wild-card game and advance
item.description: Atlanta beat Philadelphia 6-2 in the deciding third game of their wild-card series, a significant follow-up to Thursday’s opening-round results. Michael Harris II hit a three-run homer in the first inning, while Ozzie Albies and Matt Olson also went deep. The Braves now face the Dodgers after their first winner-take-all postseason victory since 1996.

item.title: Manchester City appeals Premier League financial ruling
item.description: Manchester City has appealed a ruling that found serious breaches of Premier League financial rules, including sham sponsorship contracts that allegedly inflated revenue and reduced costs by more than £900 million. An independent appeal board will review the case. Potential sanctions discussed include points deductions, relegation and removal of titles.

item.title: Cowboys acquire Joey Porter Jr. from Steelers
item.description: Dallas acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after his contract talks with Pittsburgh reached an impasse. The Steelers receive a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, according to reports. Porter, a 2023 second-round selection and son of the longtime Steelers linebacker, gives a struggling Cowboys secondary an immediate reinforcement.

item.title: Yankees, White Sox and Padres sweep into division series
item.description: Three wild-card series ended in two-game sweeps. The Yankees routed Boston 9-2, the White Sox beat Houston 7-3 for their first postseason series victory since 2005, and the Padres topped the Cubs 4-1. Philadelphia forced a decisive Game 3 with a 10-inning win over Atlanta.

item.title: Senate sends sweeping college-sports bill to the House
item.description: The Senate passed the Protect College Sports Act 77-22, proposing national rules for athlete compensation and transfers, new scholarship and health protections, and limited antitrust protection for the NCAA. The measure faces an uncertain path in a House that is out until after the midterm elections.

item.title: NFL tells Rams a decisive pass-interference flag was wrong
item.description: Sean McVay said the NFL acknowledged that Rams cornerback Josh Wallace should not have been flagged late against Denver. The penalty erased an interception and gave the Broncos a first down; Bo Nix scored the winning touchdown six plays later. The admission sharpens the perennial debate over reviewable judgment calls.
